summary.text: Matthew Orr is the Republican candidate for North Carolina House of Representatives District 33 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Monika Johnson-Hostler (D). He is an entrepreneur and executive director of the Scott Orr Foundation.

paragraphs.text: In a Ballotpedia survey, Matthew Orr said he was born and raised in South Raleigh and graduated from Garner Magnet High School.
Ballotpedia lists service in the U.S. Army from 2015 to 2016, an associate degree from Wake Technical Community College in 2019 and a bachelor's degree from North Carolina State University in 2022.

He said he earned bachelor's degrees in political science and public relations, built a career in marketing and finance, and then left the corporate world to start two small businesses that he still owns.

Orr said he serves as executive director of the Scott Orr Foundation, a nonprofit focused on mental health, suicide prevention and housing and resources for veterans, coached wrestling at South Garner High School, and lives in Garner.
He advanced from the Republican primary on March 3, 2026, which was canceled.
His stated priorities include expanding well-paying jobs and workforce pipelines with community colleges and trade schools, and ensuring fair access to resources across schools in the district.
